text:
Allergies:
Patient recorded as having No Known Allergies to Drugs

Chief Complaint:
Right femur fracture

History of Present Illness:
___ is an ___ yo female with PMH of anemia, recurrent 
UTI's, multiple prior falls brought to ___ after a fall 
and found to have R femur fracture, was tranferred here for 
ortho eval and likely surgery. Patient reports being in her 
usual state of health this morning and was walking around her 
kitchen with her walker getting ready for work. She reports 
losing her balance and falling backward. She denies any 
lightheadedness or vertigo or loss of consciousness. She reports 
having multiple prior episodes similar to this in which she 
loses her balance, resulting in falls. She denies hitting her 
head or having a headache and reports knowing she broke her leg 
as soon as she fell to the ground. Otherwise she denies any 
fever, chill, recent cold or flu like symptoms, chest pain, 
dyspnea, vomiting, diarrhea, change in appetite.  
.  
At ___ she was found to have three part significantly 
displaced and angulated subtrochanteric fracture of proximal 
right femur. She was transferred here for ortho eval and likely 
surgery. She was given morphine 4mg IV x1, 2mg IV x1 and zofran 
4mg IV. She was on NS at 150 cc/hour for unknown total amount of 
IVF administered.  
.  
In the ___ ___, initial VS: 97.7 80 151/95 16 100% 3L NC. On 
arrival she was hypoxic to 85% on room air, with increase to 98% 
on 4L NC. She is A&Ox3. EKG showed NSR, no ischemic changes. 
X-rays showed R proximal femoral shaft fracture. CT head head 
was done which had wet read of "Right parietal linear 
hypersensity likely artifact, however subdural bleed not 
excluded." This was overread by attending radiologist who felt 
that it was most likely artifact and repeat CT only if clinical 
concern. CT neck showed did not show any fracture but did note 
incidental finding of left palatine tonsil area inflamation or 
fluid collection. CTA chest was done given the hypoxia which 
showed "Subtle hypodensity in subsegmental branch of LLL pulm 
artery (3:27) may be artifactual but can't exclude a PE." 
Orthopedics was consulted and placed in traction. Plan for 
surgery tomorrow if medically cleared.  
.  
Currently, she is resting comfortably and awakens easily to 
voice. Right leg with traction in place. She reports very slight 
discomfort in her leg but reports that is significantly 
improved.  
.  
ROS: Denies fever, chills, night sweats, headache, vision 
changes, rhinorrhea, congestion, sore throat, cough, shortness 
of breath, chest pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, 
diarrhea, constipation, BRBPR, melena, hematochezia, dysuria, 
hematuria.

Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT & PLAN: ___ is an ___ yo female with PMH of 
anemia, recurrent UTI's, multiple prior falls admitted with 
displaced right femur fracture s/p mechanical fall now POD from 
TFN with multiple subsegmental PEs.  
.  
# Displaced Right Femur Fracture: s/p ORIF with trochanteric 
fixation nail. Patient's dressings were not changed until POD#2 
per Ortho recommendations. Incision sites were clean and intact 
but continued to put out serosanguinous drainage, as well as 
sanguinous drainage from right medial thigh site. Patient's 
hematocrit trended down on ___ per below and she was 
transfused another 1 unit pRBC with CT pelvis demonstrating mild 
edema but no overt hematoma. Patient required only minimal 
morphine (1mg) with transfers and responded well to tylenol. She 
was also on a vigorous bowel regiment and calcium/vitamin D. 
Patient was followed by physical therapy, weight bearing as 
tolerated, and discharged to rehab once medically stable. 
- Continue pain control with Tylenol standing (for now) and 
Morphine PRN with bowel regimen of Senna/Colace
- Continue Vitamin D/Calcium 
- Patient has outpatient follow-up in Orthopedics Clinic with 
Dr. ___ on ___ at 10:45am. She has an hip Xray 
ordered to be done that same day BEFORE the appointment, at 
10:25am.  
.  
# Subsegmental PEs - Repeat CTA showing new LLL/RUL subsegmental 
filling defects. Patient continued to have an oxygen requirement 
of 2L nasal cannula but was able to be weaned to 1L on ___ and 
then off completely. She was otherwise asymptomatic. Patient was 
monitored on telemetry and started on therapeutic doses of 
lovenox (70mg SC q12hours) with bridge to coumadin. She was 
started on Lovenox on ___ and started on Coumadin 5mg ___. 
On day of discharge, she was day 4 of Lovenox, day 3 of Coumadin 
(first day of 3mg) but day 1 of being at a therapeutic INR. 
Of note, patient also had pulmonary nodules on CT that will 
require ___ month follow-up as outpatient 
- Patient requires Lovenox 70mcg twice daily on ___, 
___ and ___. She also requires Coumadin 3mg, 
on-going. Please check INR as well as hematocrit daily from 
___ - ___ and modify Coumadin dose accordingly. 
Goal is for INR to  be 2.0-2.5 given recent surgery.
- Continue to monitor respiratory status (for tachypnea, 
tachycardia, low grade fevers, new oxygen requirement) 
suggestive of worsening or repeat PEs
- Patient requires ___ month outpatient follow-up imaging of 
pulmonary nodules incidentally seen on CT chest
.  
#Left palatine tonsil inflammation - Incidental finding on CT 
neck. Final read 1.4 x 0.9 cm left palatine tonsil hypodense 
structure may represent inflammation, evolving phlegmon or fluid 
collection. Post-contrast CT scan showed 1.5cm fluid density 
w/out inflammatory changes. No abnormalities on exam and patient 
asymptomatic. ENT recommended outpatient follow-up. 
- Follow-up appointment with ENT physician, ___ 
___ on ___ at 1:20pm 
.  
#. Iron deficiency anemia - Got 1 unit of pRBC on night of 
admission and 1 unit in the OR. HCT 31.1 -> 36.6 after 1 unit in 
OR but then returned to ___-op and trended down 29.4 --> 
28.9 --> 26.5. Patient received another unit of pRBC with 
appropriate response and once her hematocrit was stable 
(Hct>28), she was started on coumadin. Of note, patient also 
with bruising on back side of leg and right lateral lower tongue 
(? secondary to intubation/extubation trauma in the OR), on 
chronic iron supplementation for unclear etiology. Patient's 
long-standing ferrous sulfate was held as she remained 
constipated >7 days perioperatively (also on low-dose morphine). 
Ferrous sulfate was resumed once her bowels were regulated. 
- Continue Ferrous Sulfate 325mg daily
.  
#. Troponin leak: Troponin peaked at 0.05 and was 0.04 prior to 
OR. Troponin trended down further to 0.03. EKG stable from 
previously, with T wave inversion in AVL still present but T 
wave inversion in I now resolved and flat. Pre-op beta-blockade 
was discontinued. Patient had initial tachycardia 
post-operatively, felt secondary to rebound tachycardia, pain, 
known pulmonary emboli. She was monitored on telemetry X48+ 
hours without incidence (other than PVC runs). 
- Patient's primary care provider can consider starting baby 
aspirin at a future date
.  
#Systolic murmur - ___ and radiating to axilla/clavicles, 
consistent with aortic stenosis and confirmed by PCP. Last ECHO 
was in ___, demonstrating normal left ventricular function and 
gradient ot 25. Valve area was 1.5 and patient did not have 
evidence of heart failure on exam. No additional cardiac imaging 
was performed during this hospitalization. 
.  
# Right parietal linear hyperdensity: Was on initial CT head but 
repeat CT head showed no bleed. Attending radiologist also 
confirmed that hyperdensity is likely an artifact. 
.  
# Hiatal hernia: Noted on CXR and CT chest but patient remained 
largely asymptomatic. Patient was started on pantoprazole given 
size of hernia.
- Continue Pantoprazole  
.  
# Liver hypodensity - Seen incidentally on CT scan and felt 
likely to be a cyst. Patient remained asymptomatic and stable.  
.  
# Urinary Incontinence/frequent UTI's: Initial urine culture 
showed proteus mirabilis and klebsiella (<100,000) which was 
pansensitive except for the klebsiella's resistance to macrobid. 
Given the "dirty urine" urinalysis both times, however, it was 
felt that the initial urine culture was likely contaminated. 
Patient's foley was removed on ___ and she was continued on 
prophylactic Macrobid.
- Continue prophylactic Macrobid (nitrofurantoin)
.  
# Macular degeneration: Stable while in-patient. Patient's 
travaprost was substituted with xalatan eyedrops while in-house 
as the former is non-formulary. Patient's occuvite was also 
switched to multivitamin.   
- Resume home Travaprost and Occuvite at rehab
.  
# FEN: Patient was initially on ___ normal saline at 100cc/hour 
to maintain urine output, especially status post two CT scans 
with contrast. Her creatinine bumped to 1.2 for a day but 
responded well to the fluids and encouraged PO intake.  
- Continue to encourage PO intake, especially of fluids 
.  
# PPX: Was on PPI while NPO given large hiatal hernia found 
incidentally on CT chest, which was continued during this 
hospital course. Patient was also on Lovenox for her 
subsegmental PEs and a bowel regimen of senna/colace. Miralax 
was added secondary to constipation although patient known to 
have bowel movements only every 5 days at baseline.   
- Continue Pantoprazole at rehab given known, large hiatal 
hernia
.  
# CODE: Full code ___ for 48 hrs after surgery and 
then original code status of DNR/DNI was reinstated on ___ 
following discussion/confirmation with patient and daughter 
___, who is health care proxy. 
- Patient is DNR/DNI

Discharge Diagnosis:
Primary: 
Displaced right femur fracture
Bilateral pulmonary emboli
Left tonsil inflammation 

Secondary: 
Iron deficiency anemia
Hyperlipidemia,
Macular degeneration
